<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - Surya is an open-source, modular document OCR toolkit (Python library + CLI + optional interactive Streamlit apps) that provides pipelines for:  
     • Text detection  
     • Multilingual OCR  
     • Layout analysis & reading order  
     • Table recognition  
     • LaTeX equation OCR  
   - It is not a monolithic web app; rather a library with command-line scripts (`surya_detect`, `surya_ocr`, `surya_layout`, etc), Python API (`Predictor` classes), and optional Streamlit UIs.

2. High-Level File Structure & Architectural Layers  
   - Top-level:  
     • `surya/` – main Python package, subdivided by task (detection, recognition, layout, table_rec, ocr_error, common utilities, debug aids)  
     • CLI wrappers & convenience scripts: `detect_layout.py`, `ocr_app.py`, `texify_app.py`, plus `surya/scripts/` for Streamlit entrypoints  
     • `benchmark/` – benchmarking harness for each task  
     • `static/` – fonts/images for documentation & apps  
     • CI/CD: `.github/workflows/*`  
     • Tests: `tests/`  
     • Config: `surya/settings.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `pytest.ini`

3. Key Components to Diagram  
   A. Input Layer  
      - Supported inputs: image files, PDFs, Word docs, PowerPoints  
      - Preprocessing: loaders in `surya/input/*`  
   B. Core Task Modules (each as a separate “micro-pipeline”)  
      1. Detection Predictor  
         • `surya/detection/`  
         • Model: semantic segmentation (EfficientViT/Craft), heatmap → bboxes  
      2. Recognition Predictor  
         • `surya/recognition/`  
         • Models: Donut-derived encoder/decoder for line-level OCR  
      3. Layout Predictor & Reading Order  
         • `surya/layout/`  
         • Models: encoder/decoder for classifying regions, assigning read positions  
      4. TableRec Predictor  
         • `surya/table_rec/`  
         • Models: encoder/decoder for rows/cols/cells  
      5. Texify Predictor (LaTeX OCR)  
         • `surya/common/donut` + `surya/texify.py`  
   C. Shared Utilities  
      - `surya/common/` – model loaders, config readers, S3 weight downloader, polygon & bbox utils  
      - `surya/logging.py`, `surya/settings.py`  
   D. CLI & API Layer  
      - Python entrypoints (`surya/scripts/…`, console_scripts in `pyproject.toml`)  
      - User calls pipeline:  
         Input → Task Predictor → JSON + optional annotated images  
   E. Optional Interactive GUI  
      - Streamlit apps (`surya/scripts/streamlit_app.py`, `texify_gui`)  
      - Uses same Predictor classes under the hood  
   F. Benchmarking & CI/CD  
      - `benchmark/` modules run pipelines at scale, produce charts  
      - GitHub Actions for CI, benchmarks, CLA, publishing  

4. Relationships and Data Flow  
   - Arrow: User Input → Loader → [Detection] → bboxes →  
     • branches to [Recognition] for text OCR  
     • branches to [Layout] for region classification & reading order  
     • branches to [TableRec] for table cell extraction  
     • branches to [Texify] for LaTeX if equations are cropped  
   - Each Predictor uses shared utilities (`common`) and model configs, downloads weights from S3 as needed  
   - CLI scripts orchestrate these calls; Streamlit UIs wrap the same pipelines  

5. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
   - Modular monolith / plugin-style: each OCR task is a self-contained subpackage  
   - Pipeline pattern: sequential processing stages, with clear inputs/outputs (JSON schemas in `schema.py`)  
   - Shared core utilities for DRY (config loading, logging, bbox math)  
   - Config-driven: `surya/settings.py` + environment-variable overrides  
   - Optional compilation flags for JIT compiling PyTorch models  

6. Technologies, Frameworks, External Services  
   - Python 3.10+, PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers / Donut, timm, EfficientViT  
   - Streamlit for interactive UIs  
   - S3 (via `surya/common/s3.py`) for model weight hosting  
   - CI/CD: GitHub Actions  
   - Packaging: Poetry (pyproject.toml)  
   - Testing: pytest  

7. Tailoring the Diagram (Open-Source Toolkit Focus)  
   - Emphasize the core functional modules rather than a client-server split  
   - Show the CLI/API layer feeding into module pipelines  
   - Highlight extension points: new tasks plug into `surya/common` loaders and follow the Predictor interface  
   - Illustrate optional GUI on top of same APIs  

8. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Components should be boxes with clear labels (e.g., “Detection Predictor”, “TableRec Predictor”)  
   - Use directional arrows for data flow (Input → Loader → Task → JSON/Image Output)  
   - Color-code by layer:  
     • Green: Input/Preprocessing  
     • Blue: Core OCR/Analysis Modules  
     • Orange: Shared Utilities & Config  
     • Purple: CLI/API & GUI  
     • Gray: CI/CD & Benchmarking  
   - Use a consistent shape for models (e.g., rounded rectangles) and for utilities (e.g., hexagons)  
   - Annotate external dependencies (PyTorch, S3) with icons or small font notes  

9. Essential Elements to Capture  
   - All five task modules as separate components  
   - Shared common utilities & config layer  
   - CLI entrypoints vs Python API  
   - Streamlit GUI as an alternative front end  
   - Benchmarking harness & CI/CD pipeline  

By following these steps and focusing on the modular, pipeline-based architecture of Surya, you will end up with a clear, accurate system design diagram that captures the toolkit’s structure, data flows, and extension points.  
</explanation>
